subject: planner: return NULL for empty scalar COUNT/HAVING subquery after decorrelation (#66809)
summary: Reviewed this commit vs its first parent, focusing on planner decorrelation for scalar aggregation subqueries. The change fixes a semantic bug where decorrelated plans could return default aggregate values (e.g. COUNT->0 via IFNULL) even when HAVING should filter the aggregate row out (scalar subquery must yield NULL). It does so by detaching pulled-up HAVING predicates from join conditions and applying them after defaulting via a projection that conditionally NULL-ifies inner columns. Also adjusts BIT_AND’s default constant to use an unsigned BIGINT type, aligning with expected semantics. Checked relevant callers/helpers (Apply decorrelation, ColumnSubstitute/Schema.Clone) and later history up to `upstream/master`; no further changes found. No remaining Blocker/High issues identified (no tests run per constraints).
